pages.title: Transcendental Crystal
pages.text: Pi, e and their relatives: numbers no polynomial with integer coefficients will ever produce. Almost every real number is transcendental, yet proving any particular one is hard. The crystal never repeats its pattern, however closely you look, and it seems to go on past its own surface.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)I only ever found these in the Platonic Realm, tucked in Euclid's vaults and Hilbert's archives. No machine of mine can build one from algebra alone, which is exactly what transcendental means.

Made in $(item)Analytic Continuator$().$(br2)$(thing)Mined$(): from $(item)Transcendental Ore$(), in veins through the Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Found in$(): Euclids Vault, Hilbert Archive chests.$(br2)$(thing)Unlocked by$(): The Platonic Realm.$(br2)$(thing)Used in$(): Crystal of Transcendence, Entangled Bus Bar, Fractal Core, Golden Ratio Glass, Omnipotence Dust, Pleroma Crystal, Real Continuum, Transcendent Glass.
